extracted.intended_audience: Directorate-General for International Partnerships staff, EU Delegations and external service providers producing digital content
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating web and social media content for the EU Directorate‑General for International Partnerships that is adaptable across channels and consistent with the EU International Partnerships verbal and visual style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values-driven, impact-focused communication
rubrics_metrics.description: As a European Union institution, we showcase our work through positive, inspiring and challenging communication, which is values-driven and impact-focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should reflect EU values and emphasise impact; language and messaging must align with the institution's mission and moral framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multichannel adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines cover content created for web and social media, but we respect a multichannel approach: content created according to these guidelines should be adaptable to other non-digital formats, including, but not limited to, op-eds, speeches, factsheets, publications and internal communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce content with reuse in mind — ensure text, visuals and structure can be repurposed for print, speeches, factsheets and internal materials without losing clarity or tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and producer alignment / consistency with EU International Partnerships verbal and visual style
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines are designed to support the Directorate-General for International Partnerships, EU Delegations and external service providers to produce powerful, contemporary and consistent digital content, which reflects the EU International Partnerships verbal and visual style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All content should follow the established verbal and visual style (see the complementary Digital Style Guide). Ensure consistency across producers and channels so messaging and appearance are recognisably EU International Partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone of voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Our tone of voice is decisive, communicates positive progress and inspires action for what we need to do next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decisive language, highlight progress and call to action; avoid tentative phrasing that weakens perceived impact or urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look and feel / Visual style
rubrics_metrics.description: Our visual style allows us to communicate with impact and clarity. It reflects both modernism and heritage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (layout, typography, colour, imagery) should prioritise clear, high-impact communication while balancing modern design with respect for institutional heritage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging content that connects with the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it’s informative, inspiring or emotional, we focus on engaging content which connects with our audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an emotional register (informative, inspiring or emotional) appropriate to the objective; aim to connect with audience needs and interests rather than presenting only institutional perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography style: journalistic and un-orchestrated
rubrics_metrics.description: We look at the world with a journalistic, un-orchestrated and investigative eye. Powerful photography captures people’s attention and invokes emotion in the viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise candid, documentary-style images that feel authentic and investigative; choose photos that evoke emotion and tell human-centred stories rather than staged stock imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video: human-centred or information-driven, communicating what and why
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether human-centred or information-driven, video plays an important role in communicating not only what we do, but why we do it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use video to explain activities and motivations: human-centred storytelling or clear information‑driven pieces are both acceptable. Ensure videos reveal purpose and impact, not only facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity with the Digital Style Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: They complement the EU International Partnerships Digital Style Guide (PDF - 6MB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these guidelines alongside the full Digital Style Guide for detailed verbal and visual rules (typography, tone examples, technical specifications).
